bullets.title: NVDA: Consensus expects ~$94-95B FQ2 beat, ~$107-108B FQ3 guide; price hikes 15%+ on next-gen chips
bullets.body: Multiple banks (UBS, JPM, Rosenblatt, Cantor, Citi, Wolfe) converge on NVDA beating FQ2 revenue by $3-4B to $94-95B and guiding FQ3 to $107-108B, with some buyside expecting $110B+. NVDA is notifying customers of 15-17% price hikes on Vera Rubin/Grace Blackwell starting early 2027 due to rising memory costs; intent is to sustain 70s% gross margins. Path to $15+ EPS in C2027E and $20 in C2028E flagged by UBS; Cantor reiterates Overweight/$350 PT citing underweight investor positioning; Rosenblatt Buy/$325 PT.

bullets.title: NVDA: $6B Poolside investment + Perplexity stake signal move into model layer
bullets.body: NVDA offering $6B license of Poolside's Model Factory plus hiring 109 engineers to build Nemotron as a US open-weight alternative to Chinese models (DeepSeek, Kimi). Separately considering a multi-billion equity stake in Perplexity at $30B+ valuation. NVDA also filing to spend up to $105B supporting SB Energy Ohio data center for OpenAI's 20-year 10GW deal, and investing $1B in Poolside at $12B pre-money.

bullets.title: MRVL: Wells Fargo raises PT to $310 from $240; buyside expects 15% sequential revenue beat on Google ASIC expansion
bullets.body: Wells Fargo raised MRVL PT to $310 from $240. JPM and UBS model data center revenue +124% YoY in FY27; buyside expects ~15% sequential growth with guide up ~12%. MRVL's expanded Google custom-silicon TPU partnership ($120B revenue potential over 5.5 years per Wolfe) is seen as transformative; custom AI ASIC business modeled to more than double to $4B in F28. Stock at 35x F28 EPS vs AVGO/NVDA in teens; positioning score 1/5 (light).

bullets.title: DRAM/NAND surge: contract DRAM +58-63% q/q in Q2; NVDA warns customers of 15%+ cost hikes; MU/SNDK big Q2 winners
bullets.body: DRAM spot prices rose 5-11% monthly; contract prices surged 58-63% q/q in Q2 after a 90-95% jump in Q1. Q2 NAND revenues of top five producers rose 77% q/q to $68.7B, with MU up 99.2% to $11.9B and SNDK up 50.7% to $9.0B. TrendForce expects server DRAM contracts to rise another 13-18% in Q3. SNDK is down 9.8% and WDC down 7.4% in Canadian morning trading, reflecting broader pre-market semiconductor weakness.

bullets.title: WULF: Kentucky PSC approves 482MW power deal; Citi maintains Buy with $31 PT (98% upside)
bullets.body: TeraWulf received Kentucky PSC approval for a 482MW power agreement for its Justified Data Campus, clearing the path for project financing and validating its brownfield redevelopment strategy. Citi's $31 PT implies 98.2% upside from $15.64, based on a DCF assuming $8.5B in 2035 revenues at 74% EBITDA margins. WULF is phased: 35% online by end-2027, 35% by 1Q28, 30% by mid-2Q28. Rated High Risk due to leasing execution and financing dependence.

bullets.title: APP: eCommerce client store growth accelerating to 2.8% WoW; intl outpacing US for 5th straight week
bullets.body: AppLovin Ads reached 11,596 eCommerce clients as of Aug 21, up 2.8% week-over-week. US stores grew 2% to 5,318 while international markets led—Hong Kong +4.4%, UK +5.2%. QTD 3Q26 average weekly store growth is 1.5% but accelerated to ~3% in the last two weeks. Citi maintains Buy on APP.

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi maintains Buy; QTD CCU data implies $1.68B bookings, above guidance high end
bullets.body: Week 34 average peak CCUs were 16.1M, flat sequentially but down 31% YoY. However, QTD CCU trends imply bookings of $1.68B, above the high end of 3Q26 guidance ($1.57-1.65B) and Visible Alpha consensus of $1.61B, at $51 bookings per payer. Citi reiterates Buy.

bullets.title: OKTA pre-earnings: strong setup with $793M Q2 revenue expected, options imply ~13% move
bullets.body: OKTA consensus preview shows Q2 revenue of $793M (in line with $790-794M guidance), non-GAAP EPS $0.97, and FCF of $161.5M. The stock is up 37.4% since May 28 vs S&P 500 +1.2%. OKTA has beaten revenue and EPS consensus in 20 of the past 20 quarters. Options market implies ~12.9% post-earnings move.

bullets.title: CLS: UBS upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $430 from $410
bullets.body: UBS analyst David Vogt upgraded Celestica (CLS) from Neutral to Buy and raised the price target to $430 from $410, signaling increased conviction in the data center supply chain beneficiary.

bullets.title: CRWV: 22V bullish on compute scarcity thesis; survey shows durability conviction falling but 2-year intent solid
bullets.body: 22V sees CRWV as an attractive entry after shares fell 25% from post-earnings highs, recommending Jan 120 calls with implied vol at yearly lows. Contracted compute prices surged from $10-12M/MW-yr to $25-50M/MW-yr. A QSG survey shows CoreWeave usage rising but 12-month investment increase intent dropped to 43% from 90%; 85% still expect to increase investment over two years.

bullets.title: SPOT: upsizes buyback by $1.5B in latest shareholder capital return action
bullets.body: Spotify upsized its repurchase program by an additional $1.5B, as noted in StreetAccount's weekly dividend and buyback summary for the week of Aug 17-23.

bullets.title: CEG/VST: power/IPP stocks under pressure; VST pausing Texas data center development on grid audit
bullets.body: Power/IPP stocks averaged -6.9% last week on AI trade unwind. VST fell 8.1% as a short contributor after pausing Texas data center development pending an ERCOT grid audit. CEG moved to 'bench' after a -3.3% decline; MS Energy notes the selloff is unrelated to fundamentals, and the ERCOT 765kV transmission delay is a positive catalyst for PSP holders (HUT, WULF).

bullets.title: AAPL: Tim Cook's final full week as CEO; foldable iPhone expected Sept 9 launch
bullets.body: This is reportedly Tim Cook's last full week as Apple CEO. The foldable iPhone is expected to launch September 9 per Mark Gurman, though it reportedly lacks telephoto and Face ID. Foldables are 1.6% of global smartphone shipments but over 50% share in China with 10M+ units sold.

bullets.title: TSLA: 5% Friday rally stalls at 50-DMA; OPCO sees positive signals
bullets.body: TSLA rallied 5% on Friday but pulled back at its 50-day moving average, a key technical level to watch this week. OPCO's industrials/macro note flagged positive signals on TSLA specifically.

bullets.title: MCHP: unusual options volume 1,125% above average with extreme bullish call bias (P/C ratio 0.01)
bullets.body: Microchip Technology saw 271,838 options contracts trade vs a 24,168 average, representing 1,125% above-average volume with an extremely bullish call-heavy skew (put/call ratio of 0.01). No specific catalyst identified in the alert.

bullets.title: INTU: UBS models 12.4-12.9% GBSG growth vs Street's 14%; Piper Sandler has Underweight
bullets.body: UBS forecasts FY27 GBSG growth of 12.4-12.9% Y/Y vs the Street's 14%, and revenue growth of 10.4% vs consensus 11.1%. May 2026 pricing changes lift Online Ecosystem growth to 17.3% Y/Y. Piper Sandler's Billy Fitzsimmons maintains an Underweight rating on INTU heading into the earnings callback webinar on Aug 26.

bullets.title: NFLX: in preliminary talks to host Peacock and Fox on its platform
bullets.body: Netflix has held early-stage discussions about integrating third-party streaming services—including NBCUniversal's Peacock and Fox's standalone app—directly into its platform, per NYT reporting.

bullets.title: WDC/SNDK pre-market weakness: down 7.4%/9.8% respectively amid broad semiconductor selling
bullets.body: Pre-market trading showed WDC down 7.4% to C$25.95 and SNDK down 9.8% to C$35.00. Broader semiconductor and storage names also under pressure: COHR -5.7%, LITE -5.3%, ALAB -4.6%, MU -3.6%, CIEN -3.3%. Klein characterizes the selling as technical/quant-driven rather than fundamental, expecting a reversal post-NVDA earnings Wednesday.

bullets.title: BABA: AI models hit 3B downloads in 6 months, surpassing Meta and Google; $10B share sale weighing on stock
bullets.body: Alibaba's open-weight AI models accumulated over 3 billion global downloads in six months, making it the world's #1 AI model by downloads, eclipsing Meta and Alphabet. Separately, BABA priced a ~$10B share sale with shares dropping post-announcement. Hedgeye notes BABA in macro context only.

bullets.title: VZ: Evercore ISI bullish after CFO meeting; $9B cost efficiency target, AI pivot underway
bullets.body: Evercore ISI sees good momentum in Verizon's growth transformation following a meeting with the CFO. The company is targeting $9B in additional cost efficiencies through 2027-2028, pivoting toward AI and tech enhancements, and restraining promotional activity to improve margins. Satellite competition is expected to remain limited in urban areas.
